I’m still doing the same wheat-maize rotation on my 10.1 mu. That’s what I know best, and on our land it is the safest way. We need the wheat first, then after harvest I put maize in quickly, no wasting days. I only finished primary school, so I don’t calculate too finely. I mostly go by what worked before, what the neighbors are doing, and how the crop looks in the field. Last year if the wheat got enough base fertilizer and two topdressings, the heads were fuller, so this year I will not cut fertilizer too much. But cash is tight and some people in the family work outside, so I also can’t make the plan too expensive or too labor-heavy.

For wheat, I will sow in early October with a local improved variety that people around here commonly use, because it comes up evenly and I can trust it. I will put fertilizer in split applications, because if I put it all at once it is wasteful and risky. I have well water, so I will irrigate wheat a few times because in our place wheat usually needs it, especially before wintering, at jointing, and around grain filling if it stays dry. For maize, I will plant right after wheat harvest in mid-June. The turnaround is very tight, so I will keep tillage simple and get seed in quickly. Maize grows well after wheat on this land, and with one base fertilizer plus one topdress and one or two irrigations depending on rain, it should be alright. I won’t spend too much on pesticide unless I really see a problem, but I will use herbicide because weeds cost yield if I leave them.
